newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Oct 31.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ten people are thought to have drowned and 50 are missing in southern Thailand after flash floods swept low-lying areas and cut southern road and rail links. The State Railways of Thailand and the Transport Co have cancelled all trips to southern provinces as flood waters in some areas of Prachuap Khiri Khan province ran as high as three metres. (BANGKOK POST)

- Large quantities of crude oil have spilled into the sea from a tanker discharging at a refinery pier off the eastern province of Rayong. Star Petroleum Refining Co says 1,000 barrels of crude spilled during what it called a routine transfer. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Attorney General's Office has refused to budge in its showdown with the government over a land reform scandal in the southern province of Phuket, insisting that all suspects, including government officials, be prosecuted at the same time if there is enough evidence. On Tuesday night, Justice Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung went on TV to revive details of the scandal, which toppled the Democrat-led government last year, and criticise public prosecutors' handling of the case. (THE NATION)

- Thai Airways International Plc has decided not to sell the assets of its air cargo and mail department to Thai Air Cargo Co, a joint venture with private partners, but will instead allow it to handle just the cargo service activities. The new plan will avoid direct competition with the new joint venture and allow Thai Air Cargo to operate its business using Thai Airways' aviation rights. (THE NATION)

- Hyundai is considering setting up an automobile assembly plant in Thailand which will pump out several Hyundai models, ranging from the Tiburon coupe to the Accent budget car. Negotiations are under way with Hyundai Motor Company of South Korea for the setting up of a plant to produce Hyundai cars in Thailand. (THE NATION)
